sources.title: Anders Bjorner and Francesco Brenti, Combinatorics of Coxeter Groups (Graduate Texts in Mathematics 231, Springer 2005; author-hosted complete PDF)
sources.locator: Section 2.1, printed pp. 27-32; Section 2.2, printed pp. 33-36; Section 2.5, printed pp. 42-44. Read in the extracted full text; the printed pages carrying Lemma 2.2.1 (PDF pages 42-43) were additionally re-read as raw layout text so that the deleted-letter (hat) notation in the two contradiction cases could be verified. Sections 2.3, 2.4, 2.6, 2.7 and the exercises were consulted only for scope.

contents.name: Section 2.1: Definition 2.1.1, the Bruhat graph $u\xrightarrow{t}w$ ($u^{-1}w=t\in T$, $\ell(u)<\ell(w)$) and the reflexive transitive closure, with the three immediate observations (strict length increase; $u<ut\iff\ell(u)<\ell(ut)$; $1\le w$)
Section 2.1: Example 2.1.2 (the dihedral Bruhat posets) and Figures 2.3-2.4 (Bruhat graphs and posets of $S_3$ and $S_4$)
Section 2.1: Lemma 2.1.4 (covers in $S_n$ are the transpositions $(a,b)$ with no intermediate value) and Theorem 2.1.5 (the type-A two-sided rank criterion)
contents.reason: The scaffolded pair uses only the general reflection/subword description of Bruhat order; the type-A rank criterion and its monotone-rectangle proof are not among the contracted claims and would add a second type-A theory to this pair.

contents.name: Section 2.2: the definition of subword, Lemma 2.2.1 (extension of a reduced subword by one letter), with its complete proof and the two cases (2.8), (2.9)
Section 2.2: Theorem 2.2.2 (Subword Property, both directions) and Corollary 2.2.3 (independence of the reduced expression)
Section 2.2: Corollary 2.2.4 (finiteness of intervals, $|[u,w]|\le 2^{\ell(w)}$)
Section 2.2: Corollary 2.2.5 ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ is an automorphism of Bruhat order)
Section 2.2: Theorem 2.2.6 (Chain Property) and the following graded-poset remark
Section 2.2: Proposition 2.2.7 (Lifting Property) with its subword proof and Figure 2.6
Section 2.2: Corollary 2.2.8 (local configurations of covers around $w,sw,tw$)
contents.reason: The two diamond configurations of Corollary 2.2.8 are not consumed by any of this pair's contracts or its companion examples; they belong with the later interval-label and shelling machinery and are deliberately left there.

contents.name: Section 2.2: Proposition 2.2.9 (Bruhat order is a directed poset) with its proof by induction and lifting
Section 2.2: Lemma 2.2.10 (the product inequality $x<xt$, $y<ty$ imply $xy<xty$)
contents.reason: Lemma 2.2.10 is a technical input to the R-polynomial and multiplication arguments of later chapters; no claim of this pair quantifies over it and it is not needed for the subword, lifting, cover or quotient statements.

contents.name: Section 2.5: Proposition 2.5.1 (the minimal-coset projection $P^J$ is order-preserving) with its induction proof, Corollary 2.5.2 (covers over $W^J$), Corollary 2.5.3 ($W^J$ is directed)
Section 2.5: Proposition 2.5.4 (for finite $W$ the map $x\mapsto w_0xw_0(J)$ is an antiautomorphism of $W^J$)
contents.reason: Proposition 2.5.4 presumes a longest element $w_0$ of $W$; this pair deliberately asserts nothing requiring finiteness, and the antiautomorphism symmetry is not used by any scaffolded item.

contents.name: Section 2.5: Theorem 2.5.5 (Chain Property in $W^J$, including the check $w_1\in W^J$) and Corollary 2.5.6 (all maximal chains in $W^J$ have the same length)
Sections 2.3, 2.6, 2.7 (finite case and longest element; the criterion; interval structure)
contents.reason: Finite longest elements and opposition are proved at thm-cg-finite-parabolic-longest-element-and-opposition on batch17. The deletion-label shelling and full-interval Mobius specialization are separately homed on batch16. Batch12 proves general subword, lifting and grading claims and does not duplicate either later proof home.

sources.title: Tom Denton, Lifting property and poset structure of finite Coxeter groups (UC Davis MAT 280 lecture notes, 26 January 2009)
sources.locator: Complete 3-page lecture note; read in full, including the proof of Lemma 1, the proof of Proposition 5 and the proof of Proposition 7.

contents.name: Lemma 1: extension of a reduced subword of a reduced word $s_1\cdots s_q$ for $w$ to some $v>u$ with $\ell(v)=\ell(u)+1$
Theorem 2 (Subword Property): $u\le w$ iff some reduced expression of $u$ is a subword of a fixed reduced word of $w$
Corollary 3: $w\mapsto w^{-1}$ is an automorphism of Bruhat order, proved through reversal of words
Theorem 4 (Chain Property) and the following cover/rank paragraph (covers satisfy $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+1$; rank function is $\ell$)
Proposition 5 (Lifting Property) and its proof; the sentence that the lifting property characterises Bruhat order
Proposition 7: Bruhat order is a directed poset, by induction on $\ell(u)+\ell(w)$ and the lifting property

Section 2: Proposition 8 (existence of $w_0$ for finite $W$ and detection by $D_L(x)=S$), Proposition 9 (properties of $w_0$), Corollary 10 (anti-automorphisms $w\mapsto ww_0$, $w\mapsto w_0w$) and Theorem 11 (Hombergh-Waterhouse)
contents.reason: The finite-case longest-element theory of Section 2 presumes finiteness, which this pair explicitly does not; its statements are not scaffolded here and no scaffolded proof uses them.

sources.title: Carl Marberg, MATH 6150F Coxeter systems and Iwahori-Hecke algebras, Lecture 11: More about Bruhat order (HKUST, Spring 2017)
sources.locator: Lecture 11, printed pp. 1-2 in full (Sections 1-2); Section 3 was read only far enough to see that it develops the Tits cone.

contents.name: Section 1: Strong exchange condition with uniqueness of the deleted index in the reduced case
Section 1: the Bruhat order as the transitive closure of $w<wt$ for $t\in T$, and the remark $ws<w\iff\ell(ws)<\ell(w)$ for simple $s$
Section 1: the subword theorem ('for some, equivalently every, reduced expression')
Section 1: the lifting lemma ($us\le v$ or $us\le vs$) and the covering lemma with its use of the lifting property
Section 1: the chain proposition with its complete two-case induction and the corollary that $(W,<)$ is graded with rank function $\ell$
Section 2: unique factorization $w=uv$ with $u\in W^J$, $v\in W_J$, length additivity, and minimality of $u$ in $wW_J$
Section 3: fundamental domain of the $W$-action on $V^*$, the dual chamber decomposition and the Tits cone
contents.reason: Section 3 is the geometric chamber/Tits-cone material of the canonical-roots and Tits-cone pairs of this run; the combinatorial Bruhat-order pair neither states nor consumes it.

sources.title: Grant T. Barkley, Bruhat order and applications, Lecture 3 (CMND lecture notes, author-hosted)
sources.locator: Lecture 3, printed pp. 1-2 in full (Sections 1-2 as far as the Gale order), plus the closing problems list inspected for scope.

contents.name: Definition 0.1: Bruhat order by the existence of a reduced subword in a reduced word for the upper element
Definition 1.1: the Bruhat graph with edges $u\to v$ when $u=tv$ and $\ell(u)<\ell(v)$
Proposition 1.2: the strong exchange, exchange and deletion properties as previously proved inputs
Theorem 1.3 ($u<v$ iff there is a path in the Bruhat graph) and its proof
Lemma 1.4 (existence of $u'$ with $u<u'\le v$, $\ell(u')=\ell(u)+1$, with the 'last missing letter' argument) and Corollary 1.5 (covers raise length by one)
Corollary 1.6 (one fixed reduced word of $v$ suffices to test $u\le v$)
The observation that $u\le_R v$ (weak order) implies $u\le v$ (Bruhat order), with the $S_3$ comparison
Section 2 (Gale order and the two-sided type-A rank criterion), Section 3 (Bruhat decomposition and rank matrices) and the problems list
contents.reason: The Gale/tableau criteria and the Bruhat decomposition of $GL_n$ belong to the Lie/Schubert side of the library; this pair is confined to the general Coxeter order and its $S_4$ examples.
